Test the best single model CWT_rf to see if a single strong model beats the median baseline.
Test a weighted combination on the most stable pool (pool1) using inverse error weights to see if it outperforms best_single.
Test a weighted combination on pool1 using inverse_error to see if a focused weighted set improves over best single.

Test a simple median over the moderately stable pool3 to see if a broader set improves over median pool1.
Test a robust dynamic Bayesian averaging (dba) on pool2 to see if it can outperform the best single model.
Test a weighted combination on the larger pool3 to see if expanding the set improves over the current best single model.
Test a trimmed_mean on the best pool5 to see if trimming improves over pure weighted.
Test a simple mean over pool5 to see if averaging beats the weighted version.
Test a weighted combination on pool4 using the best_per_horizon weighting method to see if focusing on horizon-specific best models improves over current leader.
Evaluate a trimmed mean over pool4 to see if trimming improves over plain mean and weighted.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool5' (an agent proposal) as the best of 22 backtested attempts, score 0.3756. Series context: trend strength 0.9257 and seasonal strength 0.3314; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.407); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 8.021.
